hidden/x: A two-layer network starts like a linear classifier. Here the input, x, has two entries: one and two.
hidden/W1: The first layer's weights, W one, have one row per hidden unit. Each row is one neuron's weights, so this layer is two neurons side by side.
hidden/z: Dot each row with x, and add the biases, b one. Unit zero: two, minus two, plus one, is one. Unit one: one, minus four, plus zero, is minus three.
hidden/h: Then the ReLU, entry by entry: one stays one, and minus three becomes zero. That is h, the hidden layer: h is the ReLU of W one x, plus b one.
scores/W2: The second layer scores h exactly as a linear classifier scores an input, with its own weights, W two, and biases, b two: s is W two h, plus b two.
scores/s: Class zero: three times one, plus one times zero, plus zero: three. Class one: minus one, plus zero, plus one: zero.
scores/forget: Skip the ReLU, and h would be one and minus three. Class zero would score zero, not three. The bend changes the answer.
scores/shapes: The shapes chain together. Write D for the number of inputs, H for the number of hidden units, and C for the number of classes. W one is H by D: it turns D inputs into H hidden units. W two is C by H: it turns those into C scores.
collapse/sub: Take the ReLU out and substitute. The scores are W two times W one x, plus b one, plus b two. Multiply it out, and that is W two W one, the product of the two matrices, times x, plus a constant.
collapse/one: W two W one is a single C by D matrix. The two layers collapse into one linear classifier, however wide the middle is.
collapse/bend: The ReLU between them is what stops the collapse, and what lets the network bend its decision boundaries.
